findings.evidence: plot.py:18-20 define the three hex values and plot.py:35 passes them as barh colours. Measured on image-0.png the fills render at exactly (146,146,146), (176,106,44) and (46,139,87), carrying 92045, 110776 and 90768 pixels in the two plot areas, while each bar's identity is given by the y tick label set at plot.py:39.
findings.summary: The three bars are coloured grey, orange and green, but every bar is already named by its own y-axis label on both panels, so the hue carries no information a reader can use: redrawing all three in one neutral, or in lightness steps of one hue, would lose nothing. The middle hue, #b06a2c, renders as a muted orange-brown (OKLCH L 0.77, C 0.09, H 73 degrees) at the dull end of the warm-brown family the plotting style retires, so beside the clean green it reads as dirt rather than as a component. It stays non-blocking: the rows are labelled, nothing is hidden, and the figure is fully readable.

findings.evidence: The tick digit '0' of the x tick '10' occupies rows 672-681 (10 px) and '100' occupies rows 672-681 (10 px); the axis label 'warm booking tangent [ms]' occupies rows 691-703 (13 px) and the 12 pt value label '508.26' rows 564-576 (13 px). findings.summary: The script never applies the repository's data-ink style (the sibling prototype calls plt.style.use('data-ink') in its own main), so every label is drawn at matplotlib's defaults rather than the declared sizes. Tick digits carry 10 px of ink where the style's 14 pt would carry about 14 px, the axis label carries about 13 px where 16 pt is prescribed, and the value labels are set to 12 pt at plot.py:48, also below the 14 pt direct-label size. At the ~900 px reckon column that presents the page, the same tick digits fall to about 6 px, below body text -- exactly the reading cost the style's stated sizes exist to prevent. It stays non-blocking because at the delivered 1400x720 the text reads without magnification and no label is clipped or lost.

rubric_lines: RUBRIC legibility: pass. Two side-by-side linear panels titled with their device ('H200, reserved card', 'P100 on titan'); the same three ledgers on both, named 'base', 'shared kernel only' and 'shared kernel / + cut buckets'; every value printed at its bar end so no value has to be read off an axis. All text is legible at the delivered 1400x720 without magnification. One reading cost is recorded as non-blocking finding 2: the type renders below the repository's declared sizes, so at the ~900 px reckon column the text shrinks to about 6-7 px.

RUBRIC data_ink: pass. Each plot area holds three solid bars and the six value labels, and nothing else. Measured over rows 40-655 inside the two plot areas: 92045 px of grey #929292, 110776 px of orange #b06a2c and 90768 px of green #2e8b57. The only remaining non-white pixels are near-black text and spine, plus the pale antialiasing fringe of the bar edges (3676 px of light tints such as (236,219,203) and (203,226,213)); the bars carry all the visual weight.

RUBRIC decoration: pass. No gridlines (plot.py:53 calls axis.grid(False)); the top and right spines are hidden at plot.py:51-52, so the only spines drawn are the two left spines at columns 155 and 848 and the bottom spine at row 661; no background fill, panel frame, shadow or styled theme. The only furniture is the required axis text and the panel titles.

RUBRIC contrast: pass. All text is near-black on white, far above the 4.5:1 text floor, and every value label sits in white space beside its bar end rather than on the fill. The fills are graphic marks, not text: grey #929292 is 3.11:1 on white, the prescribed 'reads as data and still recedes' grey, and orange #b06a2c and green #2e8b57 are 4.25:1 each, above the 3:1 graphics floor.

RUBRIC table_form: pass. The image carries six scalars, but its job is the at-a-glance comparison a table does not give: a 20-fold device gap (27.85 against 580.32 ms on the same arm) and one arm reversing direction between devices (the shared kernel alone is 46 percent worse on the H200 and 2.1 percent worse on the P100, while the two together are 14.4 percent worse on the H200 and 12.4 percent better on the P100). The exact numbers are additionally tabulated in the same evidence fragment, so the figure is not the only form the data take.

RUBRIC label_collision: pass. Nothing is clipped and no label overlaps another label or the data. The render's ink bounding box is rows 16-704, columns 18-1384, and all four canvas edge rows and columns carry zero non-white pixels. The only two-line label ('shared kernel' / '+ cut buckets') has a clear 6 px gap between its lines (ink rows 559-569 and 576-586). Every value label sits in white space to the right of its bar; the rightmost ('592.86') ends near column 1360 of the 1400 px canvas.
